title: release.yml's registry-verification step false-fails on win32-arm64 propagation lag
description: The 'Verify the registry serves what was published' step in .github/workflows/release.yml (release.yml:165-190) polls npm for all seven packages up to 10 times with a fixed 30s sleep (5 minutes total, no backoff), then hard-fails the whole workflow run if any package -- so far always quest-win32-arm64 -- is still not visible. This is now 2 for 2 across real releases (0.4.0 and 0.5.0): the underlying npm publish succeeded both times and the package was live minutes later, but the CI run itself is marked red, which is exactly the failure mode the step's own comment (release.yml:160-164) says it exists to prevent. A red run on a successful publish trains whoever reads it to discount red runs, which is how a real failure gets missed later. Separately, the loop's error message ('still not served after 10 checks') does not distinguish 'not yet visible yet' (propagation lag, likely transient) from 'served but wrong content' (a real mismatch) -- those are different failure classes and should not look identical in the output. Deferred past the OPAG-64 fleet backlog campaign per opum-agent's instruction (2026-09-08); not urgent, does not block any release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The registry-verification loop in release.yml gives win32-arm64 (and any platform) enough total time and backoff to clear ordinary CDN propagation lag without hand-waving the window -- informed by how long 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 actually took to become visible, not guessed

The loop's output/error clearly distinguishes a package that is still not visible (propagation-in-progress, potentially transient) from one that is visible but serves the wrong content (a real mismatch), so a red run always means a real problem
Change is covered by a workflow-level dry run or documented manual verification demonstrating the new window/backoff and the distinguished failure output

plan: 1. Gather timing evidence for how long 0.4.0/0.5.0 propagation lag actually took (docs/reference/quest-cli-release-truth.md, QCLI-241, QCLI-242, QCLI-267 tracker notes) -- exact resolution timestamps are unavailable (2026-09-10 repo deletion/recreation wiped the run logs), so design conservatively off the qualitative evidence that both releases resolved shortly after the old 5-minute budget
2. Rewrite the polling loop in .github/workflows/release.yml with a longer total window and exponential backoff, sized as a documented multiple of the window that already failed twice
3. Distinguish the two failure classes in the step output: propagation timeout (still not visible) vs content mismatch (visible but wrong bytes), so a red run always means a real problem
4. Run bun run check and a YAML well-formedness check

5. Verify the new logic locally: extract the loop into a standalone script and run it under mocked npm/node against the old and new budgets side by side, proving the old one reproduces the false-fail and the new one does not, without dispatching a real publish
6. Record implementation notes and modified files, check acceptance criteria with evidence, write final summary
7. Commit, push branch fix/QCLI-247-registry-verify-propagation-lag, open PR into dev, report PR number
implementationNotes:
Timing evidence gathered before designing the fix (per the task's own instruction to check docs/log.md, this task record, and QCLI-267/QCLI-271's notes rather than guess). No exact resolution timestamp exists for either 0.4.0 or 0.5.0's win32-arm64 lag: docs/reference/quest-cli-release-truth.md's "Current publication state (2026-09-07, updated for 0.4.0)" section and QCLI-241's own implementation notes both say the publish step succeeded for all seven packages, the post-publish verification step failed after its 10x30s/5-minute retry budget specifically on quest-win32-arm64 (npm's own publish log showed "Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available"), and it "resolved shortly after on independent polling" -- no republish. QCLI-242's implementation notes record the identical shape for 0.5.0's real publish (run 34238193335): "the post-publish 'Verify the registry serves what was published' step failed only on a propagation-lag timeout for quest-win32-arm64 (10 checks not enough), not a real publish failure -- confirmed by querying the registry directly afterward: all seven packages ... show version 0.5.0". QCLI-267 independently confirms the underlying reason exact run logs from either release can no longer be retrieved for finer-grained timing: this repository was deleted and recreated on 2026-09-10 (OPAG-70), and gh run view on both cited run ids (34133338726, 34133947526) now 404s. So the fix is sized as a documented multiple of the window that already failed twice, not a fresh guess: the old budget was flat 30s x 10 (~270s of actual checks before the terminal one). The new budget is exponential backoff 15/30/60/90s x up to 12 checks, ~13m45s (825s) of total wait -- about 2.75-3x the old window, chosen to comfortably clear "shortly after" a 5-minute miss (npm's own wording is "a few minutes") without the common fast case (all seven visible on the first check, which is what happens for the other six platforms every time) waiting any longer than before.

Change: .github/workflows/release.yml's "Verify the registry serves what was published" step. (1) Replaced the flat 10x30s loop with a 12-attempt exponential-backoff loop (15s, 30s, 60s, then capped at 90s), with the step's comment citing the 0.4.0/0.5.0 evidence above and the exact new budget. (2) The exhaustion error message is now explicit that it means "never appeared under <version> in that window at all" (a propagation-class failure), names the 0.4.0/0.5.0 precedent, and explicitly states it is NOT a content mismatch. (3) The post-loop receipt-verification call (scripts/qualification/native-execution-receipt.mjs --verify-published, unchanged) is now wrapped so its failure prints an explicit "::error::registry content mismatch: ... visible ... but ... bytes do not match ... a real defect, not propagation lag" -- a second, textually distinct failure class from the loop's own message. No other step, script, or line in release.yml was touched.

Verification (no real publish dispatched, per the task's explicit instruction that this is reserved for the repo's own user): (a) `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/release.yml')); print('OK')"` -> OK. (b) `bun run check` -> typecheck/lint/format/layer-check clean, 460 pass / 0 fail (one pre-existing, unrelated lint warning in test/qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts, not touched by this change). (c) Extracted the step's exact `run:` shell block via a small python/yaml script and ran `bash -n` on it -> syntax OK. (d) Built a local harness (scratchpad, not committed) that stubs `npm`, `node`, and `sleep` and runs the extracted loop under four scenarios: all seven visible immediately (exit 0, 1 check); win32-arm64 lagging but resolving inside the new window (exit 0, resolves at attempt 7 / ~375s elapsed); win32-arm64 never resolving (exit 1, prints the new "registry propagation timeout" message, explicitly says NOT a content mismatch); all visible but the receipt disagreeing (exit 1, prints the new "registry content mismatch" message, explicitly says NOT propagation lag). All four behaved as designed. (e) A second, time-based harness reconstructed the exact pre-fix loop verbatim and ran it head-to-head against the new loop with quest-win32-arm64 scripted to become visible at a fixed real-elapsed-time point of 320s (chosen because it is past the old loop's last check at ~270s but well inside the new loop's ~825s budget, matching the qualitative "resolved shortly after 5 minutes" evidence from both real releases): the OLD loop reproduced the exact false-fail ("::error::still not served after 10 checks: quest-win32-arm64", exit 1); the NEW loop waited it out and succeeded (exit 0, "all seven packages visible on the registry (after 7 checks, ~375s elapsed)"). This reproduces the defect under the old code and shows the new code does not have it, at a resolution point directly informed by the recorded evidence.
finalSummary:
The registry-verification loop in .github/workflows/release.yml's "Verify the registry serves what was published" step was widened and given backoff, and its output now names which of two failure classes occurred.

What changed and why: the old loop was a flat 30s x 10 (5-minute, no backoff) poll that hard-failed the whole run if any of the seven npm packages was still invisible -- and it false-failed the actual publish twice in a row (0.4.0 and 0.5.0), both times on quest-win32-arm64 alone, which npm's own log describes as still "being processed" past the window even though the publish itself had already succeeded. No exact resolution timestamp survives for either incident (docs/reference/quest-cli-release-truth.md and QCLI-241/QCLI-242's tracker notes only say it resolved "shortly after" the 5-minute cutoff on independent polling; the underlying workflow run logs 404 today because this repository was deleted and recreated on 2026-09-10, per QCLI-267). So the new budget is a documented multiple of the window that already failed twice rather than a fresh guess: 12 attempts with exponential backoff (15s, 30s, 60s, then capped at 90s), ~13m45s of total wait -- about 2.75-3x the old window, while the common fast case (all seven visible immediately, which is what the other six platforms always do) is exactly as fast as before. Separately, the step's two possible red outcomes now read differently: exhausting the loop prints "registry propagation timeout: still not visible ... in that window at all", explicitly says this is NOT a content mismatch, and names the 0.4.0/0.5.0 precedent; the post-loop receipt-verification call (unchanged script, scripts/qualification/native-execution-receipt.mjs --verify-published) is now wrapped so a bytes mismatch prints "registry content mismatch: ... visible ... but ... do not match ... a real defect, not propagation lag". A red run can no longer look the same for both causes.

Verification, since dispatching release.yml with publish=true is explicitly out of scope and reserved for the repository's own user: `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` confirms the YAML is well-formed; `bun run check` is green (typecheck/lint/format/layer-check clean, 460 pass / 0 fail, one pre-existing unrelated lint warning untouched by this change); the step's exact shell block passes `bash -n`. Beyond static checks, the new polling logic was exercised directly: a local harness stubbing `npm`/`node`/`sleep` ran the extracted loop through four scenarios (immediate success; win32-arm64 lagging but resolving inside the new window at attempt 7/~375s; win32-arm64 never resolving, producing the new propagation-timeout message; all visible but a receipt mismatch, producing the new content-mismatch message) and all four behaved as designed. A second, time-based harness reconstructed the exact pre-fix loop verbatim and ran it head-to-head against the new loop with win32-arm64 scripted to become visible at a fixed real-elapsed point of 320s -- chosen because it is past the old loop's last check (~270s) but well inside the new loop's budget (~825s), matching the qualitative "resolved shortly after 5 minutes" evidence from both real releases. The old loop reproduced the exact recorded false-fail ("still not served after 10 checks", exit 1); the new loop waited it out and succeeded (exit 0). This directly demonstrates the defect under the old code and its absence under the new code, at a resolution point informed by the actual evidence rather than an arbitrary pick.

Acceptance criteria, all checked with the evidence above: (1) the loop now gives every platform ~13m45s with backoff, sized against the recorded 0.4.0/0.5.0 evidence rather than guessed; (2) a red run's message now says which class it is -- still-not-visible vs visible-but-wrong-content -- so a red run always means a real problem; (3) the new window/backoff and the distinguished failure output are demonstrated by the local harnesses described above, in place of a real publish dispatch that is explicitly out of scope for this session.

Scope: only .github/workflows/release.yml's "Verify the registry serves what was published" step (and its preceding comment) was touched. No other step, script, or workflow file was modified.
